approved: Australia Council (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2013
Regional Australia, Local Government, Arts and Sport

Introduced the companion Consequential and Transitional Provisions Bill, which will repeal the nearly 40-year-old Australia Council Act 1975 and take effect from 1 July 2013, ensuring continuity for Council staff and its chair and deputy chair during the transition to a new skills-based board.

Summed up debate on the Australia Council Bill 2013, the most significant reform of the Australia Council's legislation in nearly 40 years, citing an additional $75.3 million invested over four years bringing total funding to over $200 million a year, and detailed amendments explicitly recognising Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander arts practice, freedom of expression in the arts, and peer assessment on funding committees.

Moved a procedural motion affirming the House's actions on the Australia Council Bill 2013 and its consequential bill, noting Senate committee concerns had been addressed, and thanked the opposition for supporting the housekeeping motion to transmit the bills to the Senate.
